topic: x86-64 Assembly Programming and Function Calls
explanation: This concept focuses on writing and understanding x86-64 assembly code, particularly in the context of function calls and the interaction between caller and callee. It, highlighting the management of registers and the stack, crucial for understanding processor execution and program behavior at the hardware level. Understanding this is essential for performance optimization, debugging, and interacting directly with system hardware.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
.globl my_func
my_func:
    ; Callee Prologue (Setup Stack Frame & Save RBP)
    PUSH RBP
    MOV RBP, RSP

    ; Callee must save Callee-Saved registers (RBX, R12-R15)
    PUSH RBX

    ; RDI holds Arg1 (Caller sets this)
    MOV RAX, RDI
    MOV RBX, 5
    ADD RAX, RBX ; RAX = Arg1 + 5

    ; Callee Epilogue (Restore saved registers)
    POP RBX
    MOV RSP, RBP
    POP RBP
    
    ; Return value is in RAX (Caller reads this)
    RET
keywords: x86-64 calling convention, x86 assembly stack frame, x86-64 ABI, System V ABI
